title: SRE shift sprintstitch — tactical notes and handoff (Jan 11-12 2027)
body:
Context and purpose:
This doc is a tactical shift write-up combining the last 36 hours of on-call observations, a concise incident debrief, SLO metrics snapshot, and an explicit handoff checklist. Goal: make the night-to-day transfer frictionless and call out immediate follow-ups (0–7d) vs backlog items (7–30d).

High-level summary (what happened)
- Incident window: 2027-01-11 03:12–03:47 UTC. Root symptom: sudden spike in 5xxs for hosted inference control plane (route: /v1/infer).
- Impact: several customer burst batches experienced token-level truncation and increased latency; highest impact between 03:18–03:32 UTC. Estimated customer-visible error rate peaked at 0.88% across routed requests (hosted-api).
- Immediate remediation: roll forward to last-known-good control-plane config (rollback of autoscaler config change), restart of 3 control-plane pods in eu-west-1, and targeted KV-cache warmup for heavy prefixes.
- Status post-remed: traffic and error-rate normalized by 03:47 UTC. No long-lived data corruption observed.

Quick timeline (UTC)
- 03:12 Alert: Pager duty P1 from synthetic suite (multiple broken transactions).
- 03:15 Triage: identified control-plane autoscaler config pushed earlier that morning.
- 03:20 Action: rollback to prior config; restarted control-plane replicas; initiated cache-warm.
- 03:32 Observation: error-rate trending down; latency still elevated (P95 ~220ms).
- 03:47 All clear: error-rate < 0.05% and throughput normal.

Root cause (current hypothesis)
- A change to the autoscaler target thresholds reduced available control-plane slots during a high synthetic-burst window. This caused queueing and led to timeouts in the inference router, cascading into KV-cache warm-up storms because many requests missed cache entries simultaneously.
- Secondary factor: cache-priming logic had a narrow concurrency window that amplified regen latency.

SLO snapshot (last 7d vs target)
- Availability (control-plane request success rate): target 99.95% monthly. Last 7d observed: 99.87% (incidents contributed ~0.06% drop).
- Latency (API P95 end-to-end): baseline target 180ms. Last 7d observed: 205–230ms during bursts; median remained ~65ms.
- Mean time to mitigate (MTTM) for P1: 28 minutes (target < 30).

Customer impact notes
- Notified customer success for three impacted tenants with elevated error reports. CS ticket refs in linked_artifacts. No SLA credits evaluated yet; flagged for account review if follow-ups find repeat behavior.

Immediate action items (0–7 days)
- A1: Adjust autoscaler change workflow to require a staging soak (owner: Marco Li) — due 2027-01-15.
- A2: Add circuit-breaker for router-to-control-plane on elevated queue length (owner: Eileen Park) — prototype PR GH-PR-9987. Target review by 2027-01-18.
- A3: Widen cache-priming concurrency window to avoid regen bursts; add backoff (owner: Jordan Reyes) — merged to canary, monitor next 72h.
- A4: Runbook update: document the autoscaler rollback steps and add single-command cache-warm script (owner: Aisha Thompson) — due 2027-01-14.
- A5: Create synthetic test that simulates simultaneous cache misses at scale (owner: Samir Patel) — due 2027-01-20.

Longer-term backlog (7–30+ days)
- B1: Workload-aware autoscaler: experiment with predictive scaling using prefix frequency patterns (owner: eng-serving-runtime team, coordinator: Rosa Delgado).
- B2: Cache-priming redesign: investigate hierarchical priming and cold-primed replicas.
- B3: Capacity planning: add eu-west-1 steady-state buffer for peak synthetic windows.

Handoff checklist (for incoming shift)
- Verify alerts: check synthetic suite and error budget slack for control-plane + router.
- Run quick health probes: curl /health on control-plane pods in active regions and confirm cache-hit rate > 92% for top-100 prefixes.
- Confirm PR canaries: GH-PR-9987 and recent cache change merged to canary have healthy traces in the last 2 hours.
- Pager roster: confirm coverage for next 48 hours. Primary oncall: Marco Li (pager), secondary: Eileen Park. Contact escalations: Eng Leads — Samir Patel (infra), Rosa Delgado (serving runtime).
- Postmortem owner assigned? Not yet. Decision: if customer impact >2 tenants or incident recurrence within 14 days, convert to formal postmortem.

Knowledge / runbook gaps observed
- The autoscaler change checklist is minimal — lacks a mandatory staging-phase sign-off and perf-check.
- Cache warmup scripts are ad-hoc and not standardized per region.
- Observability: we need a dedicated dashboard that correlates control-plane replica counts, router-queue length, and cache-miss spikes in one panel.

Operational notes and small wins
- Canary rollout process worked as expected for the cache-window adjustment (Jordan's change) — canary metrics showed degraded but stable perf before rollout was paused for autoscaler rollback.
- SRE tooling: added a quick CLI alias 'sre:cp-rollback' to perform the three-step rollback for control-plane; saves ~3–4 minutes during mitigation.

Questions for triage meeting (tomorrow 10:30 PST)
- Should we require a mandatory synthetic soak for autoscaler config changes? Thresholds?
- Is the cache priming logic fundamentally brittle or just misconfigured?
- What are the minimal customer notification rules for transient P1 events?

Short-term monitoring checklist (next 72h)
- Dashboards: add alert for correlated spike pattern (router queue > 500 AND cache-miss-rate > 18%).
- Synthetic: add one synthetic that floods top-500 prefixes for 5m at region-local scale (owner: Samir Patel).
- Runbook: publish autoscaler rollback steps and test the CLI alias in staging (owner: Aisha Thompson).

Owners and acknowledgements
- Oncall (night): Marco Li — triage and primary mitigation.
- Follow-up leads: Marco Li, Eileen Park, Jordan Reyes, Samir Patel, Rosa Delgado.
- Drafted by: Aisha Thompson (shift notes).

If you're taking this shift: read this doc, ping the listed owners for status, and run the handoff checklist live on Slack in #sre-ops before 09:00 PST. If anything looks off with the dashboards, escalate to the named leads immediately.

Appendix: relevant links and tickets
- JIRA-4521 — incident tracker
- GH-PR-9987 — router circuit-breaker prototype
- confluence://sre/cache-eviction-runbook — runbook stub (needs update)
- slack://threads/C0ABCDEF/1623 — incident channel logs

Notes to self: keep this short and prioritized; move design discussions to an RFC.
